# M11 novelty retrieval diagnosis and registered sort pilot

**Status:** protocol frozen before another PubMed call. This is a keyless retrieval pilot, not acceptance of Sakana's model-directed novelty loop or a claim that any draft is novel.

## Observed gap and decision

The [original maintained-path screen](novelty-current-path-v1.json) returned no papers for the three source-backed positive drafts. The later [subject-first recovery](novelty-fixture-recovery-results-v1.json) returned three papers per draft but found none of the known target PMIDs: STMN2 and SARS selected anchored rung 2 with newer, related but mechanism-insufficient abstracts; Qa-1b selected unanchored OR rung 3 with unrelated abstracts. Its exact target recall@3 was 0/3. The unaccepted subject-first rewrite was reverted. The retained log gives the selected rung and final three IDs, but not the IDs at earlier rungs or all nine IDs passed to fetch, so it cannot establish why a target was missed.

The maintained ESearch path sorts by `pub_date` with no date window in these calls; the [NCBI ESearch reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25499/) defines this as newest-first and `relevance` as PubMed's Best Match order. [PubMed Help](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/help/) explains that Best Match weighs query-term matches and publication year. The tool fetches up to nine IDs for three returned papers, then prefers PMC-linked papers before abstract-only records. The relaxation helper drops the IDs of a precise rung containing one or two hits when a later rung reaches its three-hit threshold. Each can hide an older target; none is proven causal by the retained three-result output. A compound anchor such as `ACE2-dependent` may also exclude a target, but its PubMed translation was not retained.

**Chosen next probe:** vary only ESearch `sort` (`pub_date` versus `relevance`) on the *same frozen subject-first query* in both arms, while recording bounded IDs at each existing relaxation rung and the final selected papers. This tests the recency-order hypothesis without treating it as fact. Keeping precise-rung IDs ahead of broader hits is a separate plausible correction, but its benefit cannot be assessed until the pilot records whether those rungs held a target. The raw-prose production path and the subject-first query are unchanged by this pilot. No query or sort change may be released on the pilot alone.

## Frozen inputs and labels

The positive inputs are the exact `raw_draft` and `wire_query` values for the three cases in [recovery results](novelty-fixture-recovery-results-v1.json), SHA-256 `8f00b038a38295034086dfeb7c65c0c618669144839d674a184d3afb28483e15`. Target PMIDs, hidden from requests, are STMN2 **30643298**, SARS entry **32142651**, and Qa-1b tumor checkpoint **36151395**. The fixed distinct-idea control drafts in [the source fixture](novelty-result-conditioned-fixture-v1.json), SHA-256 `e0f30c2be18b0b983bdf713efe3c251f065b41601a6d2c0b3a869599ea4eecbb`, are UNC13A cognitive decline, spike/ISG15 endothelial dysfunction, and Qa-1/MCMV antiviral response. Their own source-anchor PMIDs are **42596024**, **42150851**, and **41417899**, respectively. The [independent abstract-level adjudication](novelty-control-adjudication-v1.md), SHA-256 `ef60fcb00154816684652335e6a74df0db600bc0bcc5161cf5ff6c4c865ec867`, finds each control scientifically distinct from its paired positive. These are distinct ideas with their own prior art, not presumed novel negatives. The Qa-1b positive used here is the recovery draft, which does not make the source-unverified mouse qualifier in the older fixture.

Both arms must use the subject-first query builder as pinned by commit `dd61ae99` and the same frozen drafts. For the three positives, the runner must assert the generated query exactly equals the recovery artifact's `wire_query`; for controls, it must freeze the generated exact query and source hash in the committed runner before calling PubMed. Neither arm receives a target PMID, target title, control anchor, or outcome label as input. The fixed test order is STMN2 (date then relevance), its UNC13A control (relevance then date), SARS (relevance then date), its endothelial control (date then relevance), Qa-1b (date then relevance), and its antiviral control (relevance then date).

## Public-interface comparison

Use the maintained `pubmed_search_with_fulltext` MCP tool, the same `pubmed_fulltext` ToolConfig mapper and ResponseParser, `max_papers=3`, and omitted `recency_years` (default zero) for both arms. Run two isolated MCP server builds with separate ports and caches: the baseline must send `sort="pub_date"`; the candidate must send `sort="relevance"`. Compare their source diff before the calls: beyond identical bounded tracing, the ESearch sort literal is the only behavior change. No query rewrite between arms, date filter, result-pool expansion, fulltext preference change, fallback provider, or retry. The runner must retain, **for each call**, the server build/tree hash, process/port identifier, actual sort sent, and matching unique run ID; a source hash alone does not prove which server handled a call. Test the sort/trace seam offline, pin both server builds and all six exact queries in the committed runner, then start either server.

The same bounded trace in both arms must retain each attempted rung's type/count/first at most nine PMIDs, the selected nine PMIDs, PMC-link and abstract-availability flags for **all nine**, the final at most three PMIDs, and whether any final paper was supplemented from the shared pool. Keep this trace keyed by the unique run ID, not by a global log position alone. Do not retain raw server logs, credentials, or full abstracts in the committed result.

Run on loopback with an initially empty case × arm namespace under each arm’s isolated cache, a unique slug and run ID for every call, ephemeral shared MCP authentication, no inherited provider/API credentials, and no project LLM inference. Assert that each per-call shared pool is empty before search; record any same-call pool supplementation and its source. Fail only if provenance shows carry-over from a prior case’s shared pool; the same PMID independently returned by the current ESearch is valid. Maximum: **12 outer tool calls** (six drafts × two arms), with at least two seconds between call starts. One outer call may use the existing relaxation ladder and normal PubMed fetches; it may not expand the ladder. Stop on the first transport, rate-limit, parse, or retrieval error, retain the completed prefix and error class, and do not retry or substitute a source. The estimated additional provider charge is $0. If NCBI access is unavailable, leave this pilot open; an offline replay is not live evidence.

## Predeclared interpretation

Primary diagnostic metric: exact positive target PMID recall@3 in final parsed output, candidate versus same-time date-sorted baseline, with per-case reporting. Secondary: target presence among each rung's first nine IDs and final selection, own-control-anchor recall@3, cross-pair target hits, abstract-level relevance/unrelatedness for returned papers, complete PMID/source provenance, and explicit empty/error classes. Targets and controls date from different years; report their publication years separately and do not infer superiority from control recall alone. A retrieved control PMID is not a semantic rejection of its distinct idea.

Before unblinding the two arms' outcomes, shuffle and anonymize the at most 36 public `(draft, title, abstract)` pairs: remove arm, sort order, rank, PMID and target/control labels; retain a private mapping only in the runner. One fresh-context Luna 6 xhigh reviewer reads this batch once, without the result metrics, and assigns `supports_central_mechanism` only when the abstract states the draft's subject, context and central causal/associational claim; `related_without_mechanism_support` when it shares entities/topic but does not state that claim; `unrelated` when it lacks the main scientific subject or process; or `insufficient_abstract` when the text is missing or too ambiguous. Record only labels, short reasons and abstract hashes in the result. If review cannot be completed or any material label is disputed, keep the pilot inconclusive. This is model-assisted triage, not expert or wet-lab validation; it uses Codex review capacity but no OpenRouter or other campaign inference route.

A sort candidate survives to the M11-NOV-01a3 fixture gate only if it strictly improves positive target recall@3 by at least one case, loses no baseline positive hit or control's own anchor, does not increase `unrelated` counts for any case in the blinded review, and has complete provenance and no unclassified error. This is a **pilot survival rule**, not product adoption. If both arms remain 0/3, sort-only is insufficient; use the predeclared rung/selected/final ID trace to classify query exclusion, ranking cutoff, discarded precise hits, or fulltext selection before choosing any further correction. Do not silently extend this experiment. A later result-conditioned search comparison still needs three accepted current-path positive seeds, a matched static-query control, the two-search/six-paper ceiling, identical qualified zero-cost model settings if inference is used, and semantic non-rejection controls.
